chunks: But we have only become fighting our brethren in Islam
because of what entered it of misguidance, crookedness, doubts and (wrong) interpretation,
if we find any way by which we may come near each other in whatever common remains between us, we would accept it, and would give up everything else.

key_terms.التَّأْوِيلِ: Interpretation (often implying subjective or wrong interpretation)
key_terms.الزَّيْغِ: Misguidance or deviation from the truth

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali fight the Kharijites and companions if he sought peace?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that the conflict with the Kharijites was a necessary measure to rectify internal deviations (zaygh) and restore Islamic unity, rather than a pursuit of personal power. He articulates a pragmatic political strategy: utilizing arbitration as a tool to draw the parties back to their remaining common ground (al-baqiyyah), thereby accepting temporary compromises to preserve the core of the faith. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of 'political realism' where ends justify means in the context of preserving the community's integrity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: We now had to fight our brethren in Islam
because of entry into Islam of misguidance, crookedness, doubts and (wrong) interpretation.

However, if we find any way by which Allāh may collect us together in our disorder and by which we may come near each other in whatever common remains between us we would accept it and would give up everything else.
